title: Identity in the Cloud: No Passwords Needed

scenes.line1: How does a VM get secrets safely?
scenes.say: How can your app or virtual machine grab secrets from the cloud without ever storing a password?

scenes.label: Identity
scenes.sub: Managed identity lets a VM authenticate to services with no password stored.
scenes.say: Azure managed identity means your virtual machine can prove who it is to other services, without any password hiding in a config file.
Azure uses managed identity and role-based access control. AWS does the same with a role attached to your instance and policy assignments.

rows.b: Attach Key Vault access to identity

scenes.say: First, assign a managed identity to your VM. Next, grant it a role, like Key Vault access. Now, the VM gets tokens on its own—no credentials needed.

scenes.question: Do you need to store secrets on the VM?
scenes.wrong: Yes, you must keep credentials there.
scenes.right: No, managed identity handles authentication and secrets access automatically.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for it: you never need to stash secrets or credentials on the VM. Managed identity takes care of authentication and access for you.
